Convert completed Deputy agent results and delegations

Source: R/deputy-adapter.R
as_trajectory_deputy.Rd

as_trajectory_deputy() snapshots one or more completed deputy::AgentResult objects, and the disclosed delegation views of a deputy::LeadAgent, into a canonical TrajectoryBundle. It delegates model-visible turns to as_trajectory_ellmer() and adds ordered, namespaced Deputy lifecycle events. Results and events are read through their public S7 properties.

Usage

as_trajectory_deputy(
  x,
  trajectory_id = NULL,
  source_uri = NULL,
  metadata = list(),
  delegations = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A completed deputy::AgentResult, a non-empty list of completed results, or a list of disclosed delegation views on its own.

trajectory_id

A bundle-unique trajectory ID. When NULL, a stable ID is derived from the Deputy run ID (or, for a delegation that never ran, its delegation ID). It must be NULL when the input holds several runs.

source_uri

An optional source locator. Credentials, query parameters, and fragments are removed.

metadata

A uniquely named list of safe application metadata, applied to every trajectory. Sensitive fields are redacted and recorded as losses.

delegations

Optional disclosed delegation views to convert beside the results in x, usually the lead result's own delegations. Use the value of deputy::delegation_history() or of lead$inspect_subagents(transcript = TRUE). A raw $export_subagents() snapshot is an error: read it with deputy::delegation_history() first, so Deputy checks your DelegationDisclosure again.

Value

A TrajectoryBundle.

Details

Run, session, agent, delegation, usage, ending, and immutable run-context values are retained as sanitized data. When a run's parent occurs in the same input, the adapter resolves parent_trajectory_id from Deputy's lineage: the parent run ID, then, for a nested delegation, the parent delegation ID. Otherwise it retains the parent IDs as metadata, leaves parent_trajectory_id missing, and records an adapter loss. Missing run identity is also explicit. Source objects, providers, tools, callbacks, and credentials are never retained.

as_trajectory() dispatches to this adapter for Deputy results and non-empty lists containing only Deputy results when Deputy is installed. Delegation views are plain lists without a class of their own, so they need this function.

Run ending

The trajectory status follows the result's RunEnding: RunEndingAnswered and RunEndingCutOff are "completed", RunEndingStopped and RunEndingLimit are "interrupted", and RunEndingFailed is "failed". A cut-off answer keeps "completed" because Deputy completed the run; the provider truncated its final response. Check metadata$ending$cut_off whenever a whole answer matters.

trajectory_info(bundle)$metadata[[i]]$ending always has these fields, in this order, with NA where the ending does not supply one:

  • class (character): "RunEndingAnswered", "RunEndingStopped", "RunEndingLimit", "RunEndingCutOff", or "RunEndingFailed".

  • reason (character): the stop, limit, or failure reason.

  • by (character): who stopped a RunEndingStopped run, such as "caller", "hook", or "abandoned".

  • field (character), actual (double), limit (double): the UsageLimits field reached, the figure reached, and the figure allowed. actual is also NA when Deputy could not know it.

  • wrapped_up (logical): for a limit, whether the model gave a final answer in the extra request allowed by on_exceed = "wrap_up".

  • phase (character): where a failed run failed.

  • finish_reason (character): the provider's finish reason for the final response.

  • cut_off (logical): whether the provider cut that response short. It is TRUE for every RunEndingCutOff and for a truncated wrap-up answer.

The failure condition itself is projected by the deputy:run_error event.

Events

Each deputy::AgentEvent becomes a deputy:<type> event, in source order. Fields that are not projected into a column stay in the event's sanitized metadata, with Deputy S7 values and conditions as plain lists.

  • tool_start, approval: value is tool_input.

  • tool_end: value is tool_result, and error is tool_error.

  • content: value is content.

  • trusted_result: value is the trusted value; result_id, result_type, and tool_fingerprint stay in metadata.

  • structured_attempt: value is the attempted value; valid, feedback, and attempt stay in metadata.

  • request_error, run_error, compaction_error: error is the condition message.

status is "failed" for request_error, run_error, compaction_error, a tool_end with an error, a denied permission, and an invalid structured_attempt; "pending" for an approval awaiting a decision; and "completed" otherwise. name and call_id carry tool_name and tool_call_id; text carries text, a start task, or a warning message.

Delegation views

Each view becomes one trajectory with source_type = "deputy". Its turns are the view's replayed ellmer turns; a view has no lifecycle events, timestamps, or run context. status follows outcome$runtime$status: "completed" and "failed" keep their names, "stopped" and "suspended" are "interrupted", and "not_started" is "cancelled". As with results, "completed" means the run ended normally, not that the task succeeded. metadata$ending has the ten fields above, with only finish_reason and cut_off set.

The view's metadata keeps the result keys session_id, agent_id, parent_agent_id, parent_run_id, delegation_id, usage (the delegation's AgentUsage fields), and stop_reason, adds parent_delegation_id, and sets source_class to "delegation_view". metadata$delegation holds:

  • task (character): the delegated task label.

  • answer (character): the subagent's final reply, which Deputy cuts to 8 KiB.

  • claims$missing_evidence, claims$unresolved_work (each character(1)): what the subagent reported in its structured output, entries joined by newlines. "" means it reported none; NA means it did not report, not that nothing is missing.

  • references (list): one record per saved artifact, with reference, source ("tool_result" or "delegation_answer"), tool_call_id, and availability: "available" or "missing" from a live $inspect_subagents() view, or "unresolved" from delegation_history(), whose saved status may be stale. References are never read.

  • manifest (list or NULL): the DelegationManifest fields schema_version, definition_id, provider, model, params, tools, policies, and size. The manifest's task, evidence, prompt, and message text are not copied.

  • runtime (list): Deputy's whole runtime record, including depth, root_agent_id, answer_truncated, and claim_omissions.

  • cumulative_usage, errors, and retention, as in the view.

Delegation losses

  • capture$transcript is "redacted" when disclosure withheld a delegation's transcript, so its turns and tool activity are absent, and "unsupported" when the view was read without one.

  • contents$value is "externalized" on each tool result, in a result or a view, that Deputy moved out of the model context: the event holds only a preview, and the loss metadata holds its reference.

  • metadata$delegation$answer and metadata$delegation$claims$<name> are "truncated" when Deputy bounded them.

  • parent_run_id or parent_delegation_id is "unsupported" when the parent is not in the same call.

Examples

if (
  rlang::is_installed("deputy", version = "0.0.0.9007") &&
    rlang::is_installed("ellmer", version = "0.5.0")
) {
  result <- deputy::AgentResult(
    turns = list(
      ellmer::UserTurn(list(ellmer::ContentText("Hello"))),
      ellmer::AssistantTurn(list(ellmer::ContentText("Hi")))
    ),
    run_id = "run-001",
    agent_name = "assistant"
  )

  bundle <- as_trajectory_deputy(result)
  trajectory_events(bundle)
  trajectory_info(bundle)$metadata[[1]]$ending

  # With a LeadAgent `lead`, convert its delegations beside its result:
  # history <- deputy::delegation_history(
  #   lead$export_subagents("reviewer"), "reviewer", disclosure, scope
  # )
  # as_trajectory_deputy(result, delegations = history)
}
